Anna R: Heads-up — nightly CI bench flagged a regression in kernel selection for llama-2-13b q4 paths on p4d. p50 up ~18% vs yesterday. Anyone on kernel selector / batching heuristics? :eyes:
Joe P: saw it. likely the fallback to generic_attention. Sequence length distribution shifted in the traffic snapshot so selector picked a safer kernel.
Tanya K: can you paste the bench run id and config? I can try a local replay.
Anna R: run id nightly-2026-03-17-23, job: nightly-inference-bench, model=llama-2-13b-q4_0, hw=p4d. Logs: https://internal.ci/runs/nightly-2026-03-17-23
bench-bot: nightly-bench summary for nightly-2026-03-17-23 — model=llama-2-13b-q4_0, hw=p4d, median_p50=134ms (+18%), p95=420ms (+22%), kernel_selected=generic_attention (fallback), batching: auto_batch=true, max_batch=64, kv_cache_hit_rate=0.31, replay_seed=8234. Artifacts: /artifacts/nightly-2026-03-17-23
Joe P: 0.31 KV hit_rate is low; that increases KV loads and can change kernel code path because of different memory patterns. Also if batch sizes were smaller the optimized kernel might not be applicable.
Liam S: I'll run the replay harness locally with the same snapshot:
```
./replay_harness --run-id nightly-2026-03-17-23 --target-qps 80 --seq-dist=recorded --kv-warmup 0.5 --preserve-prefixes 
```
Add `--kernel-policy prefer_optimized` to force the optimized kernels for apples-to-apples.
Tanya K: also try forcing batch size and disabling autoscaling in the harness to remove scheduler variability: `--max-batch 32 --disable-auto-batcher`.
Joe P: Good. On CI automation side we should: 1) rerun automatically on threshold breach, 2) collect kernel selection trace + perf profile, 3) post to perf dashboard and create PERF ticket if delta persists. Current thresholds are p50 >10% or p95 >15%.
Anna R: Agreed. Add repro steps to flaky triage: rerun with `--deterministic` + `--skip-quantize` to isolate quantization-induced variability, then run perf collector: `perf record -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- ./serve ...` and kernel selector trace: `KERNEL_TRACE=1` in env.
bench-bot: triggered rerun for nightly-2026-03-17-23 at 1720208400. Rerun flags: --kernel-policy prefer_optimized --max-batch 32 --kv-warmup 0.6. Collecting: perf, kernel-trace, batch-stats.
Liam S: Note on KV cache: replay harness must match prefix distributions or warmup will be off. Use `--prefix-preserve` and `--warmup-queries 2000`. Otherwise you get low hit rates and different memory access patterns.
Tanya K: For apples-to-apples comparisons we must normalize: same sequence length histogram, same batch policy, same tokenization config, same quantization flags. Add a small doc snippet to the bench runner config: 
```json
{
  "seq_histogram": "recorded",
  "batch_policy": "fixed",
  "max_batch": 32,
  "kv_warmup_target": 0.6
}
```
Joe P: Also add CI step to publish the rerun artifacts to Grafana as a timeseries: kernel_version, batch_size, kv_hit_rate, p50, p95. That makes regression triage faster.
Anna R: one more practical: sometimes selector is nondeterministic when two kernels have similar perf; add tie-breaker by stable kernel id to reduce flakiness.
bench-bot: rerun completed at 1720209400. Result: p50=129ms (baseline delta +5%), p95=395ms (+6%). Kernel used=optimized_attention (forced), kv_hit_rate=0.58. Creating ticket PERF-423.
deploy-bot: created PERF-423 and posted dashboard snapshot: https://grafana/internal/d/daily/nightly_inference_bench?orgId=1&panelId=3 :thumbsup:
Tanya K: next steps — add the replay command and kernel-trace collection to the nightly failure workflow, and add automatic flaky tagging if rerun reduces regression below threshold. Also add a post-mortem template for persistent perf regressions.
Joe P: I'll add a Jenkins/ci job that runs the replay locally on PRs touching kernel selector and batching heuristics. Quick smoke: `./ci/bench_smoke.sh --pr-id $PR`.
Anna R: thanks all. Let's keep the bug focused: if PERF-423 still shows delta after fix we escalate to runtime team. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Liam S: thanks — I'll attach replay logs and perf.data to PERF-423 in 30m.
bench-bot: note — added tag `nightly-alert` and subscribers: @eng-runtime, @eng-ml.
